headline: Highest risk is medium: caveman can ingest files/MCP while dagster is local-only, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways without direct execution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and reads files like CLAUDE.md/project notes, so attacker-controlled content could reach its instruction channel; dagster has no shared channel or clipboard/files, so the pairwise bridge is indirect and not proven. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF caveman is pointed at untrusted files or an MCP server that carries attacker-controlled content, THEN prompt injection is plausible.
IF dagster remains fileless and MCP-free as profiled, THEN no direct bridge exists.
mitigations: Restrict caveman to trusted directories only.
Disable MCP endpoints for caveman during review runs.
Add a manual approval step before caveman consumes new files.
Keep dagster isolated from any shared workspace.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all file-fed instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, but dagster has no filesystem read/write or API egress, so there is no documented path for those data classes to leave the pair. The main risk is local workspace exposure, not exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same writable workspace, THEN caveman's notes could be visible locally.
IF dagster is given filesystem read access outside this profile, THEN leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Store caveman notes in a separate directory.
Avoid placing secrets in project notes or CLAUDE.md.
Run dagster without added filesystem permissions.
Review logs before sharing them externally.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances, but dagster is profiled with no filesystem write, no git modification, and no subprocess or shell execution, so there is no overlapping mutable resource to conflict over. The pairwise write-conflict pathway is blocked by dagster's empty write surface.
conditions: IF dagster is later granted write or git permissions, THEN conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state, THEN the current none rating no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep dagster read-only.
Do not mount a shared writable repo.
Avoid concurrent writes from caveman instances.
Document any future permission changes before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking if write access is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can produce content that another system may treat as authoritative, and dagster is a data orchestrator that could propagate that output if wired into a pipeline. Dagster is not documented here as verifying caveman's claims, so the interaction is plausible but indirect.
conditions: IF dagster ingests caveman-generated text as pipeline metadata or task input, THEN errors can cascade downstream.
IF a verification step is inserted before dagster acts, THEN this risk is reduced.
mitigations: Require human review of caveman output before ingestion.
Add schema validation on any caveman-produced text.
Keep dagster from auto-triggering actions on free-form text.
Log provenance for all upstream content.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman explicitly touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while dagster's profile shows no data classes touched and no residency or retention mismatch. With no sensitive class or jurisdictional evidence, only a minor documentation/compliance gap is visible.
conditions: IF caveman stores regulated data in its notes or logs, THEN compliance review is needed.
IF dagster is configured to retain pipeline metadata longer than caveman, THEN retention mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in caveman notes.
Set short retention for session logs.
Review any pipeline metadata retention settings.
Confirm both tools' data handling policies before use.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
